text.p: Italian debt markets ended subdued and soggy as general EMU concerns weighed on sentiment depite reassuring noises from Brussels, and the absence of U.S. players reduced activity in the marketplace.
"For the next few weeks the problem for the market won't be 'Will Italy participate or not?' but 'Will EMU occur at all?'," said one broker at a U.S. bank in London.

With U.S. investors off for a holiday, March Btp futures on LIFFE fell 22 basis points to 130.72 while the November 2006 Btp ended 15 basis points lower at 104.38, yielding 7.24 percent and with spread over Germany of 174 basis points.

Amid a market questioning even Germany's ability to meet the EMU criteria, a senior European Union monetary union source said speculation of an EMU delay stemmed from market cravings rather than any formal plans in the EU.
But the London trader: "We must know as soon as possible whether Germany is willing. People are also fearing and doubting the political willingness of Germany over EMU."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi visiting Germany said he would not ask for softening of the criteria for Italy.
At home, industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said he saw no grim surprises for February inflation due Thursday and Friday.
Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema said an additional mini budget for 1997 was "inevitable" but would not be huge.
The lira held in a narrow range against the mark, still hugging the 987 per mark area despite dollar gains against the German currency.
